Read `README.md` and current rollout evidence first. Produce exactly one multi-wake target-policy candidate in `solver/`. Keep candidate-specific reasoning in `logs/optimize/wake_policy_notes.md`, and add or materially revise at least one evidence-backed reusable lesson in `guidance/control_experience.md` from the assigned parent, sampled solver results, and inherited logs. If no positive lesson survives the evidence, record a concrete negative result and what later workers should avoid or test. The candidate is incomplete until both files are updated. Work only inside this Phase 2 workspace.

This is the no-Bookshelf ablation: no cross-domain fish-control research shelf
is provided. Base controller proposals only on the task contract, current and
inherited guidance, sampled solver results, inherited optimizer logs, and
current rollout evidence. Do not search for or reconstruct the omitted shelf
from neighboring configurations or repository history.

I’ll first read the workspace contract and the wake-visual inspection skill, then audit the current rollout evidence and inherited guidance before touching the controller. I’ll keep all work inside this Phase 2 workspace and won’t consult any omitted or neighboring research shelf.

The visual-first skill confirms the order: anchor each keyframe sheet to its observation and metrics, compare the best finite run with the most informative failure, and write the diagnosis/hypothesis before any policy edit. I’m now inventorying only the assigned examples, inherited logs, current guidance, and candidate contract.

The four sampled outcomes are all failures, so the useful comparison is mechanism-level: the seed is the strongest finite trajectory (`min distance 8.61L`, 50.1 release units) while the unstable candidate fails in 1.92 units with enormous lateral load. I’ll verify the common prewarm sheet, then inspect those two released sheets and the two remaining left-domain variants for steering-sign/turn-rate clues.

The visual/metric cross-check exposes two distinct failures. The inherited parent (`c3…`) never establishes meaningful propulsion—its joint peaks equal the 8° steering bias, effort is only `0.69`, and it is advected `+2.17L` downstream. The seed does self-propel upstream, but saturates both rate and acceleration and turns nearly straight down. I’m checking the policy-state definitions and actuation conventions now so the candidate can recover propulsion without repeating the 18° anterior-bias instability.

The workspace also contains sampled optimizer guidance and inherited per-worker notes; these are in scope and I hadn’t yet included them in the first inventory because the absent top-level `logs/` path interrupted that listing. I’m reading the assigned parent and every sampled inherited note before committing to the mechanism.

The inherited results sharpen the candidate boundary. Three moderated controllers all stayed finite but were swept out the downstream boundary in about 16 units; the assigned parent is especially diagnostic because its 8° steering center cancels the initial 8° joint state, leaving the oscillator near an exact zero-energy equilibrium. The only upstream-moving run is the saturated seed, while sharing 18° steering with the anterior joint produced the 1.92-unit instability. Per the visual-first skill, I’m recording this diagnosis and a falsifiable middle-ground hypothesis before editing the policy.

The recorded hypothesis now keeps steering out of the propulsion state, restores a faster but nominally cap-feasible gait, and confines the unproven steering sign to a small posterior bias. I’m applying that single candidate and distilling the reusable negative lesson: “cap-feasible” reduced gaits were not merely slower—they all lost upstream authority, and one centered formulation mathematically suppressed startup.

The candidate and durable lesson are both in place. Before invoking the mandated runner, I’m auditing the exact semantic diffs and doing a lightweight joint-only envelope probe; this is controller arithmetic only, not CFD, and will test whether the nominal oscillator actually starts and whether its internal clamp dominates under representative bearing inputs.

The joint-only probe caught a real inconsistency before handoff: a `28 rad/time²` guard is below the proposed oscillator’s own `Aω²`, so it clipped about 19% of anterior commands even in calm constant-bearing arithmetic. I’m raising the policy-local guard to `30 rad/time²`—still below the `31.416` episode limit—and correcting the notes, then rerunning the probe.

The guidance checker hit the inherited rendering defect documented by prior workers: the same parent is marked “copied to guidance” twice, so it cannot resolve a unique baseline. I’m making the minimal workspace-local repair—removing only the duplicate marker from the second identical entry—then rerunning the mandated checks.

The candidate’s joint-only envelope probe is now clean: zero internal or episode-cap contacts across four constant-bearing cases over the full 300-unit arithmetic horizon. I’m invoking the workspace’s required check runner now; it will run only guidance, policy-contract, and boundary checks—no CFD.
